goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. The `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` method at line 160-162 returns true when `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. This is used in the `challenge` method (line 134) and `authenticate` method (line 113) to setup webauthn data when passkeys are enabled AND a user is identified. The original code at lines 112-115 only called `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` when `context.getUser() == null` (no user selected). The new code calls it when user IS NOT null. Looking at the diff, the change moves the passkey form setup to happen when a user IS identified (user != null), which is the correct behavior for conditional passkeys during re-authentication. The finding claims this breaks authentication when no user is identified, but the original code also didn't setup passkeys when no user was identified in the same scenario.

adjudication.rationale: In UsernameForm.java line 47, the diff shows `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called with no arguments. However, looking at UsernamePasswordForm.java in the same diff, the method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` is declared as `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` requiring a UserModel parameter. UsernameForm extends AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator (not UsernamePasswordForm), so it would not have access to this method. Even if UsernameForm extended UsernamePasswordForm, the zero-argument call would still be invalid since the method requires a UserModel parameter. This would cause a compilation error.

adjudication.rationale: The finding misreads the code. The method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true when `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. This is used in `authenticate()` and `challenge()` methods. Looking at the diff, the old code in `authenticate()` had `if (context.getUser() == null)` block containing `if (webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled())`. The new code moves the passkeys setup outside that block with `if (isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))`. For ordinary login (user == null), the old code would call `fillContextForm` inside the `if (context.getUser() == null)` block. The new method requires `user != null`, which would disable passkeys for ordinary login. However, examining the full context, the `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` method is specifically for re-authentication scenarios where user is already known. The conditional UI passkeys (autocomplete='webauthn') still work for ordinary login through the form's autocomplete attribute, not through `fillContextForm`. The finding incorrectly assumes this breaks normal passkey login, but conditional passkeys work via browser autocomplete, not the authenticator list shown by `fillContextForm`.

The method `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows new test code at lines 290-296 and 310-316 in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java that uses `catch (Exception nsee)` to verify WebAuthn elements are not present. This is indeed a bug - catching the generic Exception class means any exception (not just NoSuchElementException) would satisfy the test assertion. If there's a browser session issue, network problem, or any other exception, the test would incorrectly pass. The proper approach would be to catch only NoSuchElementException to verify the element truly doesn't exist.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the test is insufficient because it only checks 'Invalid password.' error message. However, looking at the diff, the test at line 378 (webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey) actually does verify re-authentication behavior properly - it checks for the info message 'Please re-authenticate to continue', verifies passkeys elements are available, and tests both password and passkey re-authentication flows. The setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError method is properly called in the error handling path (added in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java and AuthenticatorUtils.java). The test coverage appears adequate for the changes made, and the finding's claim about 'removing either re-authentication form attribute assignment leaves this test green' is speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone.
